Guernsey: The Channel Island with Character

Guernsey is smaller than Jersey but arguably more characterful. At just 25 square miles, it offers a dense concentration of cliff-top roads, hidden lanes, fishing harbours, and a south coast that's among the most dramatic in the Channel. The island has a strong independent identity and a pace of life that feels genuinely different from the British mainland.

Getting There

Condor Ferries from Poole to St Peter Port takes about 3 hours by high-speed. The conventional ferry takes longer but is often cheaper. Motorcycle spaces should be booked in advance. The ferry arrives at St Peter Port, Guernsey's charming capital.

The South Coast Cliffs

Guernsey's south coast is spectacularly rugged — high cliffs, sea caves, and rocky inlets. The coast road from St Peter Port west to Pleinmont passes through some of the most dramatic coastal scenery in the Channel Islands. Stop at Jerbourg Point for views to Jersey and the French coast, and Le Gouffre for a dramatic cliff-top walk.

The West Coast

The west coast contrasts with the south — long sandy beaches backed by dunes and low headlands. Vazon Bay and Cobo Bay are popular surfing beaches. Fort Grey (the Cup and Saucer) houses a small shipwreck museum. The coastal road is flat and flowing, perfect for a relaxed ride with ocean views.

St Peter Port

St Peter Port is one of the prettiest harbour towns in the British Isles. The town tumbles down a steep hillside to a harbour filled with yachts. Castle Cornet guards the harbour entrance and hosts daily noon-day gun ceremonies. The town has excellent restaurants, particularly for seafood, and Victor Hugo's house (Hauteville House) is open for tours.

Guernsey rewards those who slow down. At 35mph maximum, you have no choice — and you quickly discover that leisurely pace is exactly right for an island this beautiful.

Hidden Lanes and Interior

Like Jersey, Guernsey has a network of Ruettes Tranquilles (quiet lanes) where the speed limit is 15mph and non-motorised traffic has priority. These lanes weave between granite farmhouses, greenhouses (Guernsey was once the UK's tomato capital), and ancient parish churches. They're the soul of the island. Practical Information

  • Speed limit: 35mph maximum, 25mph in some areas, 15mph on Ruettes Tranquilles
  • Fuel: Available in St Peter Port, St Sampson's, and dotted around the island. Cheaper than the UK
  • Currency: Guernsey Pound (interchangeable with Sterling)
  • Duration: 1-2 days is enough to explore, but 3 days allows a relaxed pace
  • Food: Outstanding seafood. Try the Guernsey Bean Jar (traditional slow-cooked bean dish)
  • Climate: Milder and sunnier than the UK mainland, especially spring and autumn
keyTakeaways: Guernsey is smaller than Jersey at just 25 square miles but arguably more characterful, with a strong independent identity.
Condor Ferries run from Poole to St Peter Port, about 3 hours by high-speed craft; book motorcycle spaces in advance.
The rugged south coast from St Peter Port to Pleinmont has the most dramatic scenery, with cliffs, caves and rocky inlets.
St Peter Port is one of the prettiest harbour towns in the British Isles, with Castle Cornet and Victor Hugo's house.

faq.q: How do I get to Guernsey by motorcycle?
faq.a: Condor Ferries run from Poole to St Peter Port in about 3 hours by high-speed craft, with a slower but often cheaper conventional ferry available too. Motorcycle spaces should be booked in advance. The ferry arrives at St Peter Port, Guernsey's charming capital and the natural starting point for exploring the island.

faq.q: What is the best part of Guernsey to ride?
faq.a: The south coast is spectacularly rugged, with high cliffs, sea caves and rocky inlets. The coast road from St Peter Port west to Pleinmont passes some of the most dramatic scenery in the Channel Islands. Stop at Jerbourg Point for views to Jersey and the French coast, and Le Gouffre for a dramatic cliff-top walk.

Like Jersey's Green Lanes, Guernsey has a network of Ruettes Tranquilles, quiet lanes where the speed limit is 15mph and non-motorised traffic has priority. These lanes weave between granite farmhouses, greenhouses and ancient parish churches, and they are the soul of the island.

faq.q: What are the speed limits and where is fuel?
faq.a: The maximum speed limit is 35mph, dropping to 25mph in some areas and 15mph on the Ruettes Tranquilles, so leisurely riding is the order of the day. Fuel is available in St Peter Port, St Sampson's and dotted around the island, and it is cheaper than on the UK mainland. The Guernsey Pound is interchangeable with Sterling.

faq.q: How long should I spend on Guernsey?
faq.a: One to two days is enough to explore, but three days allows a relaxed pace. Do not miss St Peter Port, one of the prettiest harbour towns in the British Isles, with Castle Cornet guarding the harbour and Victor Hugo's house open for tours. Seafood is outstanding, so try the traditional Guernsey Bean Jar.
